title: finding(packages): no @object-ui package ships a 'use client' banner, so every App Router consumer must wrap each import in a client file of their own
body:
Filed by the `domain:devx @ objectui` execution seat (PM session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`, 2026-09-07T14:41Z), handed back as an observation by the #8160/#8161 dev, which could not file it itself (that dispatch forbids writing labels). ⛔ No `domain:*`, type or grade set — triage's. Dedup: local grep over the REST listing of open issues for `use client` / `server component` / `app router` hit only #8161 (this observation's origin) and its control fired.

## The reading

No `@object-ui/*` package carries a `'use client'` banner — not in source, and not in built output.

| surface | `'use client'` occurrences |
|:--|--:|
| `packages/app-shell/src`, `packages/providers/src`, `packages/plugin-view/src`, `packages/react/src` | **0** |
| the same packages' built `dist` (measured by the dev on a built tree) | **0** |
| control: `apps/site/app` | 8 files |
| control: repo-wide | 75 files |

The zeros are readings, not a broken grep: the same invocation returns 8 and 75 on the controls.

## Why it is worth a card

It is the root cause of a dead control on #8161 — that card offered `packages/app-shell/src` as its non-empty control and it was empty, because these packages never had a banner to find. But the consequence is bigger than one card's instrument:

**Every Next.js App Router consumer must wrap each ObjectUI import in a client file of their own.** Under the App Router each module under `app/` is a server component by default and the directive is per-module, not inherited, so a package that ships no banner cannot be imported directly from a server component — the context providers and hooks fail at runtime. PR #8358 makes `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` teach exactly that, so the documentation is correct either way; this card is about whether the packages should carry the banner themselves.

## Why it is filed as an observation rather than a defect

Nothing is broken today for a reader who follows the docs. Whether the published packages SHOULD ship `'use client'` is a product decision about what the packages claim to support — under the startup-focus principle it is a capability claim, not an obvious fix — and it has consequences a seat should not decide alone: a banner changes how bundlers treat the package for every consumer, including those not using the App Router.

Adjacent, and deliberately not folded in: #7912 and #7483 (the `any` seam on the same integration path), #8160/#8161 (the documentation face, closing via PR #8358).
